_comment: The Roman target board: the shortlist of exoplanets Roman's coronagraph could plausibly
see in reflected light, and the launch it is waiting on. Curated by hand and kept OUT of
planets.json — like data/tours.json, the WORDS live here and the planet data is re-joined
against the catalogue of the moment on every build (pipeline/roman_board.py).
IMPORTANT — the `catalog_id` field. The published target names and our planet ids do NOT
always slug-match: the paper's 'pi Men b' is 'HD 39091 b' in the Archive's composite table
(id hd-39091-b), and 'psi 1 Dra B b' is 'psi1 Dra B b' (id psi1-dra-b-b). This is exactly
the alias problem docs/roman-measured-data.md flags for ingestion day, so the join is by an
EXPLICIT id written here, never by slugging the display name. A target with catalog_id null
is genuinely absent from our catalogue and renders as an unmodelled slot.
Deliberately NOT recorded here: the per-planet P_access percentages from the source paper's
Table 4. They are real numbers in a real paper, but transcribing 26 of them by hand invites
a wrong digit sitting on the page forever. The board instead shows the maximum angular
separation it computes itself, from the semi-major axis and distance already in each record.

mission.name: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
mission.launch_note: NASA set this date in June 2026, pulling the launch roughly eight months ahead of its earlier commitment of no later than May 2027.
mission.after_launch: The coronagraph is a technology demonstration, switched on after commissioning rather than on day one. NASA has not published fixed dates for individual target observations, so this board counts down to the launch — the one date that is announced — and nothing more.

instrument.dark_hole_note: Roman's coronagraph works in an annulus — a 'dark hole' — from about 0.15 to 0.45 arcseconds around the star. Closer in, the starlight is not suppressed; further out, the instrument stops looking.
instrument.contrast_note: Its tech-demo requirement is raw contrast better than 1 part in 10 million inside that annulus.

source.title: Catalogue of exoplanets accessible in reflected starlight to the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
source.counts_quote: At our reference wavelength λ = 575 nm, the number of Roman-accessible exoplanets in the optimistic, intermediate, and pessimistic CGI scenarios is 26, 10, and 3, respectively.
source.all_scenarios_quote: HD 219134 h, 47 UMa c, and eps Eri b are the only planets that would be accessible in all three scenarios with P_access > 25%.
source.note: The list below is that paper's Table 4 — planets whose host stars are brighter than V = 7 and whose chance of being observable exceeds 25% under optimistic assumptions. The paper does not enumerate which ten make up its intermediate scenario, so this board does not guess: it marks only the three it names as accessible under every scenario.

targets.name: eps Eri b
targets.note: The nearest of the lot, and the widest-swinging: at its furthest it opens out past the coronagraph's outer edge.

targets.name: HD 62509 b
targets.note: Pollux — the brightest star with a known planet, and one of the brightest stars in the sky.

targets.name: HR 5183 b
targets.note: On an extraordinarily stretched orbit, which swings it right across the coronagraph's working range.

targets.name: pi Men b
targets.note: The Archive's composite table calls this one HD 39091 b — the same planet under its catalogue name.

targets.name: HD 156411 b
targets.note: The hardest case on the list: even at its widest it stays well inside the coronagraph's inner edge.

targets.name: HD 100546 b
targets.note: A young giant still embedded in its birth disc, far enough out that it glows with its own heat as much as it reflects.

targets.name: tau Cet e
targets.note: Not carried in the Exoplanet Archive's composite-parameters table for our data release — the signal has been contested since — so we have no parameters to model a colour from.

targets.name: HD 114613 b
targets.note: Likewise absent from the Archive's composite-parameters table for our data release, so there is nothing here to colour.
